clue.text: Bedclothes used as ropes

definitions.meaning: the cloths spread on a bed
on a yacht, the lines controlling a sail

explanation.surface: Someone escapes through a window down knotted bedding.
explanation.definitionFit: Bed linen is laid in these flat cloths, and on a sailing boat the lines that trim the sails go by the same name.

clue.text: Hurry to put people out of work ?

definitions.text: Hurry to put people out of work ?

parts.words: Hurry to put people out of work
parts.note: dismissing staff is 'giving the bag'; a dash with legs in bags is the picture

explanation.walkthrough: To 'sack' is to fire workers and a 'race' is a hurry, so a rush to fire people is the sports-day event run in sacks.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports-day race run with legs in bags combines dismissal (the bag) and a dash.

clue.text: The scholar takes ages to sum up

parts.note: eras are ages

indicators.note: in a down clue, 'up' reads the word from bottom to top, backwards

explanation.surface: A learned man is slow to give his summary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns SUM into MUS in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch Renaissance humanist is a famous scholar.

clue.text: The sign of a cry-baby perhaps

definitions.text: The sign of a cry-baby perhaps

parts.words: The sign of a cry-baby perhaps
parts.note: the mark a weeper leaves on the cheek

explanation.definitionFit: The mark left by weeping on a face shows that someone cried.

clue.text: Habitual shopper ?

parts.note: one who shops at a place out of custom, i.e. habitually, read through the word's root

explanation.walkthrough: The word for a regular buyer contains 'custom', meaning habit, so 'Habitual' points at its origin.
explanation.definitionFit: A buyer is called this because they come to a shop by custom, which is habit.

clue.text: Novel residence for a pawnbroker (cat included) ?

indicators.note: the cat is included within the residence's words

parts.note: the pawnbroker is called 'uncle', and his residence is a cabin
a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A fictional home for a moneylender, with a cat thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: A pawnbroker is nicknamed 'uncle' in British slang. 'Novel' looks like an adjective for the residence, but it is the definition: Harriet Beecher Stowe's book.
explanation.definitionFit: Harriet Beecher Stowe's anti-slavery book is a famous work of fiction.

clue.text: Set me another form of riddle

indicators.note: the words 'Set me' are to take a different shape, rearranged

explanation.surface: A request to be given a different puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'riddle' looks like a puzzle, but here it is a sieve, and so is the old word this answer gives.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a sieve, and to riddle is to sieve.

clue.text: She made her name in drama

indicators.note: the letters of 'in drama' are made into her name

explanation.surface: An actress found fame on the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' rearranges IN DRAMA; fittingly, the heroine of The Tempest bears this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name, Prospero's daughter in The Tempest, can stand for 'She'.

clue.text: Go back for a statistical report

definitions.meaning: an official ... of figures, such as a census or tax form

explanation.definitionFit: To revert is to come home again, and an official form of figures filed, as for tax or census, has the same name.

clue.text: Did they serve to solve any thorny problems ?

definitions.text: Did they serve to solve any thorny problems

parts.words: Did they serve to solve any thorny problems
parts.note: thorny problems are those of a flower with thorns, the badges of York and Lancaster in fifteenth-century conflicts

explanation.walkthrough: The badges of the two sides were a white and a red flower with thorns, so a thorny problem is a dispute between those flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: The fifteenth-century English civil conflicts were named after the white and red flower badges of York and Lancaster.

clue.text: It could be a ranch cab!

definitions.text: It could be a ranch cab!

indicators.note: says the following letters might be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A wagon on a cattle ranch serving as a taxi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges the letters of 'a ranch cab'; the result is an old-fashioned motor coach used for outings, which a ranch cab might well be.
explanation.definitionFit: An old motor coach for day trips is a vehicle, as a ranch cab would be.

clue.text: Some rituals holding a certain value

indicators.note: the words 'Some rituals' hold the run inside them across the word join

explanation.surface: Certain ceremonies are said to have a particular worth.
explanation.definitionFit: Worth or excellence is value in a thing.

clue.text: Old king seems to wander after his god

indicators.note: the shuffled letters come after the god's name

parts.note: Ra was the Egyptian sun god, the god of an Egyptian king

indicators.note: letters that wander move about out of their order

explanation.surface: An ancient pharaoh appears to roam in pursuit of his deity.
explanation.definitionFit: Several pharaohs of ancient Egypt bore this name.

clue.text: Twelve times a king made her cross

definitions.text: Twelve times a king made her cross

parts.words: Twelve times a king made her cross
parts.note: Edward I set up a dozen memorial crosses for his dead queen along her funeral route; 'cross' looks like anger

explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' reads as angry, but it is the monument: Edward I put up twelve crosses, one at each night's stop of his queen's coffin on its way to London.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward I's queen is honoured by the twelve memorial crosses he built where her coffin rested.

clue.text: Artist leaves a dose that was fatal to Caesar

indicators.note: the artist departs from the dose's word, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: cascara is a laxative bark, given as a dose
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter walks away from the poison that killed Julius Caesar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' takes RA out of CASCARA. The conspirator in Shakespeare's Julius Caesar struck the first blow.
explanation.definitionFit: This Roman conspirator stabbed Julius Caesar first among the assassins.

clue.text: Paper for the ignoramus?

definitions.meaning: a traditional large size of writing sheet
a hat belonging to a fool, as a dunce's headgear

explanation.surface: A sheet of stationery suitable for a dunce.
explanation.definitionFit: A large size of writing sheet takes its name from a jester's-hat watermark, and a dunce or fool would wear such a hat.

clue.text: He can truthfully say "I follow you"

definitions.text: He can truthfully say "I follow you"

parts.words: He can truthfully say "I follow you"
parts.note: 'I follow you' usually means 'I understand', but here it means 'I come after you in office'

explanation.definitionFit: One who takes over a post after another literally comes after them.

clue.text: Slow pace-makers, but All-Muggleton batsman's made about 50

indicators.note: the batsman's name goes about, around, the fifty

parts.note: Podder was a batsman for All-Muggleton against Dingley Dell in Dickens's Pickwick Papers; the 's adds S
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Dull runners, yet a cricketer still scored around fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts L (50) inside PODDERS. The cricket match in Pickwick Papers is between All-Muggleton and Dingley Dell.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who trudge along make slow progress, setting a slow pace.

clue.text: Forks out of a trunk

parts.note: 'Forks out' looks like paying up, but means limbs dividing from a tree's main stem

explanation.walkthrough: 'Forks out' suggests paying money from a box; the trunk is a tree's.
explanation.definitionFit: Limbs splitting off a tree's main stem divide, or fork, from it.

clue.text: Estate agent with genuine eminence in the States

parts.note: real means genuine
a tor is a rocky hill, a high point or eminence

explanation.surface: An American property seller of real distinction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the States' marks the word as American usage.
explanation.definitionFit: The American term for one who sells houses.

clue.text: Nearly everyone goes by taxi to the party

indicators.note: the shortened word sits beside the taxi, after it

parts.note: a cab is a taxi

indicators.note: nearly the whole word, so its last letter is cut

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: Almost all the guests arrive at the celebration in cabs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' here means a small secret faction, not a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A small secret political faction, a clique, is a party in that sense.

clue.text: A bold front giving a Red Indian endless trouble

indicators.note: the warrior's word loses its final letter

parts.note: a brave is a Native American warrior
ado means fuss, trouble

explanation.surface: A show of courage that causes a warrior unending bother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts BRAVE to BRAV.
explanation.definitionFit: Swaggering show of daring is a bold front put on.

clue.text: Took part in a running match

definitions.text: Took part in a running match

parts.words: Took part in a running match
parts.note: not a race: a couple run away together to marry, a match made on the run

explanation.definitionFit: Lovers who ran off secretly to wed made a match while running.

clue.text: This jacket doesn't suit the gardener

definitions.text: This jacket doesn't suit the gardener

parts.words: This jacket doesn't suit the gardener
parts.note: the jacket is not clothing but a crane-fly grub named for its tough skin, which eats lawn roots

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures clothing; a leatherjacket is the grub of the crane fly (daddy-long-legs), which eats grass roots and is the gardener's enemy.
explanation.definitionFit: The tough-skinned crane-fly larva, a lawn pest, is named after this hide material plus 'jacket'.

clue.text: Principal character gets a quarter of the bird

parts.note: the hero is the main figure in a story
N, north, is one quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: The leading man is handed a portion of the poultry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarter' suggests a fourth part of the bird; it is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-legged wading bird of rivers.

clue.text: Third man has a way to become a lover

parts.note: Abel, after Adam and Cain, was the third man in Genesis
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A man who came third finds his route to romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Third man' suggests the film; it is Abel, the third human in the Bible after Adam and Cain. The scholar was famous as Héloïse's lover.
explanation.definitionFit: The medieval philosopher is remembered for his love affair with Héloïse.

clue.text: Saintly victim of a much-quoted robbery

definitions.text: Saintly victim of a much-quoted robbery

parts.words: Saintly victim of a much-quoted robbery
parts.note: the saying 'rob one apostle to pay Paul' names the first apostle as the one robbed

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'rob Peter to pay Paul' means settling one debt by running up another.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostle is the one robbed in the proverb about paying Paul.

clue.text: Hull should look this way, à la Bristol

definitions.text: Hull should look this way, à la Bristol

parts.words: Hull should look this way, à la Bristol
parts.note: Hull is not the Yorkshire city but a vessel's body, and the phrase '... and Bristol fashion' means neat and trim

explanation.walkthrough: Hull and Bristol look like two English ports; the hull is a vessel's, and 'Bristol fashion' completes a stock phrase for tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel's body kept trim is neat, as in the phrase about Bristol fashion.

clue.text: A plague, though a necessity for certain developments

definitions.meaning: one of the plagues sent on Egypt in Exodus, three days without light
developing photographic film needs a room without light

explanation.surface: An affliction that is nevertheless required for some processes.
explanation.definitionFit: Absence of light was one of the ten plagues of Egypt, and photographic film is developed without light.

clue.text: Smartens up — for the stalls ?

definitions.meaning: stable hands who look after horses in stalls

explanation.surface: Someone tidies themselves before a night at the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: To spruce up is to tidy, and stable lads who tend horses in their stalls bear the same name.
